title: Reliability: platforms, lifecycle, network, keys
goal: Close the reliability gaps found after the onboarding work: run on macOS and Linux with CI on all three platforms, a full install lifecycle (update, uninstall, stale-config and untested-version warnings), lanes that survive network drops, sleep and crowded models, and keys encrypted at rest on Windows.
now: Closed: reliability work shipped as 0.2.0; ca.mjs split deferred

decisions.text: User asked to queue and close as much as possible. No WSL, Docker or gh on this machine: Linux and macOS are proven through GitHub Actions only.

Wave 3 hit the MaaS limit of 1M tokens per minute with 4 flash lanes: portable failed, vault and netwait were stopped. Root cause in the runner: CodeArts aborts a turn after its own 429 retries and the runner counted that abort as a normal interruption. Fixed (RATE_WAIT_S budget), proven against a new fake CodeArts server (checks/ratelimit.check.mjs), synced; the three lanes resumed in place.

Wave 3 merged with lead fixes; cold-start rehearsals (Codex, opencode on GLM 5.3, Claude Code) passed setup and a first feature; CI green on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows; Office hot-desk robots clickable. Wave 4 (split runner/ca.mjs) deferred: internal refactor, no user-facing gain, risky right after a release.
Plan closed: reliability work shipped as 0.2.0; ca.mjs split deferred. Dropped, never started: split.

risks: Four lanes touch runner/ca.mjs in different places: merge conflicts resolved by the lead.
Real network drop and laptop sleep cannot be produced here; netwait is proven with injected probes and a simulated tick gap.
DPAPI keys are bound to the Windows user: a profile restore on another machine needs ca auth again (the error says so).
